regime_context: The detector shows a single dominant, well-durable trend theme — Memory/HBM & Storage — atop a top-heavy semiconductor-led leadership stack, with 20 of 49 themes eligible versus 41% breadth (narrowing rotation). Crowding is prominent among the leaders (Memory, WFE, Cybersecurity, Non-AI Tech) but this is a size-down caution only, never a fade. The one validated edge is the absolute-trend gate (drawdown control); theme momentum rank is rank-IC ~0 (focus lens only). Directional accuracy in my track record is only 50.6%, so conviction stays low.
emerging_watch: Watching whether AI Infrastructure (rank 2, eligible, crowded=false) closes the margin gap to Memory/HBM & Storage — the current margin is 0.417 with narrowing breadth of rotation (0.41). I am watching for AI Infrastructure's score to overtake Memory/HBM & Storage while its durability_bar holds above 0.5; that confirmed handoff would retire this watch.

theses.subject: Memory, HBM & Storage
theses.thesis: The leading theme has the highest score, is eligible (passes the absolute-trend gate), carries a 'trend' Hurst tag and a 'confirming' val_state, making it the core trend-following candidate for staying-power risk control rather than return forecasting. Crowding (z=1.17, crowded=true) is a sizing caution but explicitly not a reason to fade the leader.
evidence: eligible=true and headline val_state='confirming' (trend gate leg)
theses.dissent: Cross-sectional momentum rank has ~zero forward edge on clean sectors, and crowding/attention spikes often mark tops — the leader is vulnerable to a sharp mean-reversion that the gate cannot predict, only blunt.

falsifier.text: SMH turns down before the check-by date and Memory/HBM leadership hands off to a non-semiconductor theme with rising breadth

theses.subject: Cybersecurity
theses.thesis: Cybersecurity is eligible, carries a 'trend' Hurst tag, and shows the single best breadth reading in the eligible set (0.5), suggesting the trend is internally cohesive rather than one-name-led. It is crowded (z=1.93), so this is a size-down candidate rather than a high-conviction add.
evidence: breadth=0.5, highest among eligible themes (cohesion leg)
theses.dissent: High crowding (z=1.93) is the most extended reading in the ranked list, and extended thematic ETFs historically mark attention-spike tops; the breadth support could evaporate quickly.

falsifier.text: CIBR breadth collapses below 0.2 while the theme loses eligibility before the check-by date

theses.subject: Robotics & Automation
theses.thesis: Despite being eligible, Robotics & Automation carries a 'mean-revert' Hurst tag with a durability_bar (0.42) below its own gate threshold, signalling weak trend health. The absolute-trend gate is the one validated edge, so leaning away from an eligible-but-mean-reverting theme is the disciplined read.
theses.dissent: Mean-reversion in the Hurst sense could cut either way, and the theme is not crowded — an unloved theme can quietly build a base and turn into the next leader; avoiding it risks missing an early regime change.

falsifier.text: BOTZ resumes a persistent uptrend with rising durability_bar above 0.5 and holds eligibility through the check-by date
